message.content:
This is a CBP ruling on an Under Armour boy's shoe. The upper is 53% textile and 47% rubber/plastics by external surface area, so the textile material predominates and the upper is classified as textile. The outer sole is rubber or plastics.

The foxing-like band matters. A foxing-like band encircling at least 50% of the shoe's perimeter makes the shoe "footwear with foxing or a foxing-like band" under HTSUS 6404.11, which covers sports footwear. Under 6404.11 (tennis shoes, basketball shoes, gym shoes, training shoes and the like), such shoes would be subject to the foxing provisions, but those apply to 6404.11 and 6403/6405 only if specific conditions are met. Here the shoe is a slip-on, so it is not covered by the "sports footwear" description unless it is athletic. The Turbo Go is a running-type athletic shoe, which points to 6404.11.

Alternatively, the shoe could fall under 6404.19.

In the 6404.11 breakdown, the code 6404.11.90 covers other items, and 6404.11.20 covers footwear with open uppers. Within 6404.11.90, the statistical suffixes cover men's, boys', and youths'.

The 6404.11 provisions: 6404.11.20 is "Having uppers of which over 90 percent of the external surface area is rubber or plastics", 6404.11.40 is "Footwear with open toes or open heels; footwear of the slip-on type, that is held to the foot without the use of laces or buttons, ... " and 6404.11.90 is "Other". The slip-on type with a foxing-like band would be in 6404.11.60 / 6404.11.80 / 6404.11.90, depending on value. Because the value is over $12 per pair, it falls under 6404.11.90 (Other), with the suffix 6404.11.9060 for boys'.

On balance, the shoe could instead be a non-athletic slip-on under 6404.19.  But the athletic running-style description favors 6404.11.

6404.11.9060 is my choice.
